title: Cartwise Shopper Payouts Earnings Ledger — Batch Credits, Debits and Negative Balances
content:
The unpaid earnings balance of a Cartwise Shopper Payouts account is fed by the batch records of Cartwise Shopper Batches. This ledger rule states how each batch earnings row reaches that balance.

## Ledger rule

(a) Every batch pay, tip, tip increase and adjustment row is credited to the payout balance once, and every batch tip reduction and pay reversal row is debited once, each keyed by its own batch earnings row and for the same amount as that row.

(b) Credits and debits flow in every payout account status, including frozen, because they record earnings rather than move money.

(c) A debit may take the balance below zero. A negative balance is recovered by offsetting the next credits: the plan's negative-balance offset percentage of each new credit is applied to recover it.

(d) Credits reach the balance on posting.

(e) Each batch earnings row reaches the balance exactly once.

## Clause no longer in force

The former clause under which, on plans making tips cashable only once their batch is finalized, tip credits counted toward the cashable balance only once their batch was finalized, is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current basis and is not applied. The plan's tip-finalization setting remains a figure of each plan.

## Evidence and object

- The question whether a batch row has already reached the balance is answered from the payout account's own entries: an earnings credit or earnings debit already booked for that same batch earnings row means the row has reached the balance, and it is not booked again.
- The amount booked is the amount of that batch row; a shopper's recollection of a different amount does not change it.

## Direction of each batch row

| Batch row | Effect on the unpaid earnings balance |
|---|---|
| Batch pay | Credit, once |
| Tip | Credit, once |
| Tip increase | Credit, once |
| Adjustment | Credit, once |
| Tip reduction | Debit, once |
| Pay reversal | Debit, once |

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical figures)

1. A balance of 12.00 receives a pay reversal debit of 20.00; the balance becomes minus 8.00. Being negative is permitted by the ledger.
2. On a hypothetical plan whose offset percentage is 100, the next credit of 15.00 is applied in full toward the negative balance: minus 8.00 plus 15.00 leaves a balance of 7.00.
3. A tip reduction row arrives while the payout account is frozen; it is debited all the same.

superseded_clauses: Where tips_cashout_after_finalization is true, tip credits count toward the cashable balance (payout_msr_cashable_balance) only once their batch is finalized.
